author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Belmont voters are expected to consider a $5.5 million expansion of the town library at the 2027 Town Meeting. The proposal would add roughly 5,300 square feet to the nearly century-old building at 146 Main Street, expanding the current 2,200-square-foot facility to about 7,500 square feet.

Plans call for a two-story addition behind the existing library, with a new entrance, program space, meeting room and an ADA-compliant restroom. A front-and-back elevator serving four stops would address barriers in the current layout. The design also aims to improve staff sight lines, enlarge the adult reading area and create indoor-outdoor space oriented toward the downtown gazebo.

The preliminary budget includes construction, furniture and equipment, final design and engineering, plus a $500,000 contingency. Trustees and library leaders say the building has not kept pace with Belmont’s population or the demand for programs and gathering space. Because the project would likely require borrowing, supporters will spend the coming months explaining its scope and tax implications before the warrant article reaches voters.
dek: The proposed two-story addition would improve accessibility, add meeting space and more than triple the nearly century-old building’s size.
headline: Belmont library expansion proposal carries $5.5 million price tag
